chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Adam from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no beast upon which five round trips (of Hajj) are made, except that it is among the camels of Paradise.'

key_terms.دَابَّةٍ: beast/animal (specifically one used for carrying loads or riding)
key_terms.نَعَمِ الْجَنَّةِ: camels of Paradise (a metaphorical or literal reward indicating high status)
key_terms.وَقَفَاتٍ: round trips/stops (plural of waqfah, referring to the stops made during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for an animal that performs Hajj five times?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records that any beast designated for carrying pilgrims which completes five Hajj circuits is counted among the 'camels of Paradise,' highlighting the spiritual merit of facilitating religious duty. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on the tangible rewards for those who serve the Hajj infrastructure, linking physical service to eternal status in the afterlife.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy  Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “If an animal travels for Hajj five times, it is like a camel of Paradise.”
